sources.entry: Wekan - Trello-like kanban. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: WeKan is an open-source, MIT-licensed collaborative kanban board application, similar to Trello, built with Meteor and Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: WeKan provides real-time kanban boards with swimlanes, lists, and cards, plus drag-and-drop reordering, checklists, labels, and attachments. It can import boards from many tools (WeKan JSON/ZIP, CSV/TSV, Excel, Markdown, Trello, Jira, Asana, and others) and export them in similar formats including PDF, iCal, and JSON. It includes board rules and automation (IFTTT-style), multiple board views (table, calendar, timeline, Gantt), and scrum and flow metrics such as burndown and cumulative flow. The admin panel covers login providers (SAML, LDAP, OAuth2), storage backends (filesystem, S3/MinIO, GridFS, Azure, Google Cloud), and backups. The README says it can run on SQLite via FerretDB v1 by default, or on MongoDB 6 through 9.
use_cases: migrating boards from Trello or Jira
notable: Runs with SQLite via FerretDB v1 by default, so no separate database server is needed
Imports from many tools including Trello, Jira, Asana, GitHub, and GitLab
Scrum and flow analytics such as burndown, cumulative flow, and Monte Carlo forecasts
Rules and workflow automation similar to Trello Butler and Jira Workflows
Multiple install options: Windows/Mac/Linux bundle, Snap, AppImage, Docker, Kubernetes
caveats: Needs at least 1 GB free RAM, with 4 GB recommended for production
Only the newest WeKan version is supported, and frequent updates are advised
README says there is no undo yet and recommends at least daily database backups
Non-SQLite databases vary: PostgreSQL is listed as working, MySQL/MariaDB/SAP HANA as experimental
